facts.raw_span: 2 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness
difficulty combing her hair and rising from a chair
morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
dysphagia for solids and liquids
without fever or weight loss
symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs
brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
leukopenia (WBC 2.96 × 10^3/µL)
microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL)
elevated C-reactive protein (18.8 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (109.2 mm/hr)
bilateral sacroiliitis
bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement

concepts.why: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, dysphagia, and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis, which is also supported by the presence of bilateral sacroiliitis and intramuscular edema.
The patient's history of thyroiditis and current thyroid function test abnormalities, along with muscle weakness and elevated inflammatory markers, suggest a possible thyroiditis-related myopathy.

Morning stiffness, joint tenderness, and elevated inflammatory markers are consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis, although the absence of certain typical features and the presence of others suggest this may not be the primary diagnosis.

The combination of muscle weakness, joint symptoms, and various autoantibodies, along with the absence of a clear diagnosis of a single connective tissue disease, suggests the possibility of Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.

The presence of muscle weakness, joint symptoms, and elevated inflammatory markers, along with the absence of certain typical features of other diseases, suggests the possibility of Sarcoidosis, although further testing would be needed to confirm this diagnosis.
The presence of progressive muscle weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and intramuscular edema suggests an Inflammatory Myopathy, which could be a component of various underlying diseases.

The combination of muscle weakness, joint symptoms, and various autoantibodies, along with the absence of a clear diagnosis of a single connective tissue disease, suggests the possibility of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, although further testing would be needed to confirm this diagnosis.

The presence of progressive muscle weakness and elevated inflammatory markers suggests Polymyositis, although the absence of certain typical features and the presence of others suggest this may not be the primary diagnosis.

The combination of muscle weakness, skin symptoms, and elevated inflammatory markers suggests Dermatomyositis, although the absence of certain typical skin features and the presence of others suggest this may not be the primary diagnosis.

The presence of joint symptoms, morning stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers suggests Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis, although the absence of certain typical features and the presence of others suggest this may not be the primary diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Progressive proximal muscle weakness is a hallmark of inflammatory myopathies, including Juvenile Dermatomyositis and Dermatomyositis.
rationales.F03: Morning stiffness is a common symptom of rheumatologic diseases, including Rheumatoid Arthritis and Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.
rationales.F06: Symmetric muscle weakness is a characteristic feature of inflammatory myopathies, including Juvenile Dermatomyositis and Dermatomyositis.
rationales.F08: Leukopenia can be seen in various rheumatologic diseases, including Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F11: Bilateral sacroiliitis is a characteristic feature of spondyloarthritis, which can be seen in conditions like Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis and Ankylosing Spondylitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and symmetric muscle strength reduction are key findings that align with Juvenile Dermatomyositis, which is further supported by the absence of skin manifestations not being explicitly ruled out and the presence of dysphagia and muscle weakness.
